items.text:
OpenAI is valued at $1.25 trillion as AI spending growth stalls

• OpenAI is valued at $1.25 trillion after raising another $11 billion, Bloomberg reports, while Ramp data shows AI spending flattening.
• Crusoe sold an unfinished Wyoming data centre project to Google, which plans to invest $17 billion in it.
• Meta's Muse agents can now build custom spaces, like trackers and planners, from a description in chat.

items.hook: OpenAI is now valued at $1.25 trillion, Bloomberg reports[S2].
items.text:
OpenAI is now valued at $1.25 trillion, Bloomberg reports.

• The new round raised another $11 billion and could reach $20 billion.
• Ramp says AI token spend grew just 1.5% across August and September.
• In July, that spending had grown 42% from the month before.

Our read: Cheaper AI prices may be capping how fast AI companies grow.

Your take: Is the AI money boom slowing down? Tell us in the comments.

items.text:
Google bought a troubled Wyoming data centre project and plans to invest $17 billion.

• Crusoe had planned to scale the site to 10 gigawatts of power.
• Google reportedly worried about its cost and timeline under Crusoe.
• OpenAI says it won't use NDAs with officials on data centres.

Our read: Data centre fights are now shaping where AI gets built.

Your take: Should data centre deals be made in public? Tell us in the comments.

You can now text Alexa to find and buy things on Amazon.

• Select US customers get an invite; others can join a waitlist.
• Send a photo of an item and Alexa finds similar listings.
• Amazon blocked Meta's Muse from querying its site in September.

Do this: Check what Alexa can buy for you before you turn texting on.
